newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens falls sharply in IBIS trade.
newsitem.headline: Siemens falls sharply in IBIS trade.

text.p: Shares in German electronics company Siemens fell sharply on Wednesday after the firm released what the market took as a bearish outlook statement for the 1996/97 financial year.
Siemens shares dived 5.6 percent from a day high of 80.70 marks ($53) to 75.50 marks in heavy IBIS electronic trade.

The stock then continued to tumble, dropping over seven percent, to a new year low of 74.11 marks in an overall stronger market, before recovering a little to trade down 5.27 points at 74.70 marks. Almost six million shares changed hands.
The company had earlier reported 1995/96 group net profit of 2.49 billion marks compared with 2.08 billion the previous year.
But dealers said Siemens' statement that said it saw no improvement in results for the 1996/97 financial year had prompted the sell-off.
The DAX index of 30 leading shares was up 7.58 points, or 0.28 percent at 2723.74, but was pulled down from higher levels by the Siemens loss.
